teaser.en: A rare forest relative of the 'miracle berry', found only in a handful of coastal forests in Kenya and Tanzania.
teaser.sw: Jamaa adimu wa msituni wa 'tunda la ajabu' (miracle berry), anayepatikana tu katika misitu michache ya pwani ya Kenya na Tanzania.

summary.en: Mdulu is a rare shrub or small tree of lowland coastal forest, a relative of the West African miracle berry. It is listed as Vulnerable.
summary.sw: Mdulu ni kichaka au mti mdogo adimu wa misitu ya pwani ya nyanda za chini, jamaa wa *miracle berry* ya Afrika Magharibi. Umeorodheshwa kuwa Hatarini (Vulnerable).

about.en: Mdulu is a shrub or small tree with simple, broad, leathery leaves crowded towards the ends of the branches. The small flowers grow in clusters directly on the stems, and the berries are fleshy. Pakia notes that *Synsepalum* species are recognised partly by their fluted stems (*mialo*), which have ridges and grooves running up the trunk. It is one of the few bark features Digo people use for identification.
about.sw: Mdulu ni kichaka au mti mdogo wenye majani sahili, mapana na magumu kama ngozi, yaliyosongamana kuelekea ncha za matawi. Maua madogo huota katika vishada moja kwa moja kwenye mashina, na matunda yake ni beri zenye nyama. Pakia anabainisha kwamba spishi za *Synsepalum* hutambuliwa kwa sehemu kwa mashina yao yenye mifereji (*mialo*), yenye matuta na mitaro inayopanda juu ya shina. Hii ni mojawapo ya sifa chache za gome ambazo Wadigo huzitumia kutambua mimea.

where.en: It is a rare species of lowland forest in coastal Kenya and Tanzania, extending into the Eastern Arc foothills. It is also recorded from Mozambique and Zimbabwe.
where.sw: Ni spishi adimu ya misitu ya nyanda za chini katika pwani ya Kenya na Tanzania, ikienea hadi kwenye vilima vya chini vya Eastern Arc. Imerekodiwa pia Msumbiji na Zimbabwe.

names.en: Digo: *mdulu*. Pakia records it only for Digo and gives no meaning. No Swahili name is recorded. In English it has been called the stalkless miraculous berry, after its relative *Synsepalum dulcificum*, whose berries make sour food taste sweet. Other Digo *Synsepalum* are *mtsamvia* (*S. brevipes*) and *msambwe* (*S. subverticillatum*).
names.sw: Kidigo: *mdulu*. Pakia analirekodi kwa Kidigo tu na hatoi maana yake. Hakuna jina la Kiswahili lililorekodiwa. Kwa Kiingereza umeitwa *stalkless miraculous berry*, kutokana na jamaa yake *Synsepalum dulcificum*, ambaye matunda yake hufanya chakula chenye uchachu kionje kitamu. *Synsepalum* nyingine za Kidigo ni *mtsamvia* (*S. brevipes*) na *msambwe* (*S. subverticillatum*).

conservation.en: It is listed as Vulnerable by IUCN, because it grows only in scattered patches of lowland forest that continue to shrink through clearing.
conservation.sw: Umeorodheshwa na IUCN kuwa Hatarini (Vulnerable), kwa sababu hukua tu katika vipande vilivyotawanyika vya misitu ya nyanda za chini, ambavyo vinaendelea kupungua kutokana na ukataji.

reason.en: Chitsamvia, named after the Synsepalum mtsamvia
reason.sw: Chitsamvia, uliopewa jina kutokana na Synsepalum mtsamvia

reason.en: Coast mimusops, another member of the same family
reason.sw: Coast mimusops, mwanafamilia mwingine wa familia hiyo hiyo
